newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Exxon has 100 mln bbl Gulf of Mexico find.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Exxon has 100 mln bbl Gulf of Mexico find.

text.p: NEW YORK, March 10 - Exxon Corp's 100 million barrel of oil equivalent Hoover discovery in the Gulf of Mexico confirms the massive potential of the region, but is a drop in the ocean for the company in terms of reserves.

Exxon said on Monday that the Hoover field, in which it has a 66.7 percent share and British Petroleum Co's BP Exploration and Oil Inc the rest, was just 15 miles from Exxon's existing 100 million barrel Diana discovery.

"The well, located approximately 165 miles south of Galveston, encountered more than 100 feet of net hydrocarbon pay. A project team is evaluating options for the development of Diana and Hoover," the company said in a statement.
A spokeswoman for Exxon added that a decision on how to exploit the reserves in the Hoover and Diana fields would be made later this year and declined to comment on likely costs.
The company said that Hoover and Diana would start production in the year 2000 at the earliest.
The Hoover discovery was at 4,800 feet, comparatively deep in a region where 2,800-3,000 feet is classified as deepwater.

"The deepwater in the Gulf of Mexico is the last unexplored frontier in the U.S. and this region will be dominated by majors like Exxon, Shell, Amoco and BP because they are the only people that can afford to develop it," said Fadel Gheit, industry analyst at Fahenstock & Co in New York.

Exxon's Hoover discovery comes just a week after the federal lease round for the Gulf of Mexico attracted record bids and confirms interest in an area where deepwater production of natural gas alone is set to rise to 2.34 billion cubic feet per day by 2000 from 465 million in 1995.

Exxon shares were firmer after the news, up $1-3/8 by 1400 EST at $101-3/4, in a generally firm wider market, while BP American Depositary Receipts matched gains earlier in London for its underlying shares to trade $1 higher at $138-3/8.
"For a company with reserves the size of Exxon, this is like Bill Gates winning a million dollars on the lottery," said Gheit.
Exxon has worldwide reserves of 13.7 billion barrels of oil, equivalent to 13 years output at current levels.
Key to companies like Exxon, Royal Dutch/Shell, Amoco Corp and BP is tying together as many discoveries as possible to make the cost of gathering and processing reserves economically feasible.

"These are really the only companies that can afford to extract from deepwater discoveries, the independents simply do not have the capital to put in these area," said Oppenheimer & Co analyst Bruce Lanni.

A number of deepwater leases owned by independents which have not been drilled will come out of contract this year and next and this presents an opportunity for the majors to consolidate their grip on the Gulf of Mexico deepwater.

"The independents do not have the deepwater rigs to drill these leases and companies like Amoco have made it very clear that they expect to pick up expired leases for next to nothing. It is the Seven Sisters riding again," said Gheit. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
